text: it says गर्भ एव एतच्छयानो वामदेव एवमुवाच (*garbha eva etacchayāno vāmadeva evamuvāca*) (Ai. Ā. 2-5). It says that Vāmadeva, while still lying in the womb, knew this principle and spoke it. The meaning of the above mantra is that the origins and natures of all the gods were revealed to Vāmadeva while he was in the womb, and that, although there was a bondage made of hundreds of iron bars, he slipped out of it like a Śyena bird and flew towards the earth. The purport of this passage is not easy. Śaṅkarācārya, Ānandatīrtha and Sāyaṇa, when they explain this occasion, take the purport to be that Vāmadeva entered hundreds of bodies as bonds, finally became a knower, was freed from them and attained liberation. But if the context of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka is examined, स एवं विद्वान् आस्माच्छरीरभेदादूर्ध्व उत्क्रम्यामुष्मिन् स्वर्गे लोके सर्वान्नामानाप्तामृतः समभवत्समभवत् । (*sa evaṃ vidvān āsmāccharīrabhedādūrdhva utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvānnāmānāptāmṛtaḥ samabhavatsamabhavat |*) (Ai. text: Of the god Agni, सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*) — of good wealth, one who is to be well resorted to — the संदृक् (*saṃdṛk*) (sight, glance) is श्रेष्ठा (*śreṣṭhā*), exceedingly praiseworthy; among mortals it is चित्रतमा (*citratamā*), most to be honoured and worshipped, and it is स्पार्हा (*spārhā*), to be desired by all. An illustration follows. As, for a man who desires milk, the शुचि (*śuci*) (bright, full of splendour) घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*), the heated (सप्तं (*saptaṃ*)) milk of the अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*) cow that flows forth, is desirable; ⟨NOTE:345⟩ so too the sight is desired. There is a second illustration: as, for a mortal begging for a cow, the मंहना (*maṃhanā*) of a milch cow — मंहति (*maṃhati*) is a root meaning giving — ⟨NOTE:346⟩ that is, as a gift is pleasing, so is it. The rest gives accent and derivation of सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*), स्मार्हा (*smārhā*) and देवस्य (*devasya*) (Grammar section).

text: The word न (*na*) in this ṛk does not have the sense of comparison; it has the sense of "now" (samprati). Just as the word iha means "here", yet the sentence इहैव निधेहि (*ihaiva nidhehi*) means "put it now", so it should be understood. Therefore the phrase यावनात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं (*yāvanātramuṣaso na pratīkaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:407⟩ means: for as long as, that is, for how long (only a short time) the dawn-time at the end of the night spreads, for just so long. The sentence सुपर्ण्यः सुपतना एता रात्रयो वसते मातरिश्वन (*suparṇyaḥ supatanā etā rātrayo vasate mātariśvana*) means: O Mātariśvan, the birds of fine wings, flying, hold the dawn-time. That is, "birds" here means the nights. The word suparṇyaḥ which indicates this, meaning "of various wings", conveys the sense of the various (fine) colours of the dawn-time. Therefore suparṇyaḥ means that when Uṣas rises at the end of the night, that Uṣas has various or beautiful colours. The extent of this dawn-time is very small. Since sunrise follows very quickly after the dawn-time, the dawn-time is very small in extent: the intention is, only for a very short time. The human hotṛ is inferior to Agni, the divine hotṛ; therefore the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated in a place lower than Agni installed on the sacrificial altar, performs the hotṛ's work only for a very short time, by the grace of Agni, who is of special wisdom: this is the main intention. By this the smallness of man and the greatness of Agni become evident. Since this ṛk says that the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated on the sacrificial altar, performs the hotṛ's work praising Agni, the divine hotṛ, it is clearly evident that here Vaiśvānara Agni means the earthly Agni who is praised, and not the Āditya.

text: Vāmadeva (ironically, addressing Indra): "O Indra, did not your young mother (Aditi) bear you with joy? Was it not with joy that the demoness Kuṣavā swallowed you? You broke through that demoness with joy and came out. Through you joy came to the waters too. Was it not from excess of joy as well that the demon Vyaṃsa struck you, slapping you on the cheek? But you, struck by him, grew greater than he, smote his head with the thunderbolt and crushed it to bits. All these are your valorous deeds. Even so your greatness cannot be thought small. As a well-nourished cow obtains an excellent calf ⟨NOTE:468⟩, your mother Aditi obtained you (Indra): of surpassing strength, unconquered by enemies, fulfiller of all wishes, impeller of all, able to protect yourself, moving at will. Then, when Aditi asked you, 'O Indra, my son, have Agni and the other gods abandoned your friendship?', you said to Viṣṇu, who was there: 'O friend Viṣṇu, you are all-pervading and my friend; show great valour to slay the asura Vṛtra.' Did you not say so? Besides, you seized your father by the foot, dragged him and killed him, and made your mother a widow. Can anyone else do this deed? Whether lying down or moving about, no one can kill you. Which other gods have strength and power equal to yours, or greater than yours?"

notes.question: ಹೆಸರು printed ("name"); read as ಹಸು "cow"
notes.decision: ಹಸು
